options.text: I look for the ship to Tarshish. There must be an easier assignment somewhere.
I rally my resources and go, even though I'm not sure I believe in the mission yet.
I show up faithfully, trusting that my role is to be available, not to understand everything.
I commit fully and publicly, inviting others to join me in obedience.
I embrace it with compassion, knowing that the people I'm sent to need God's mercy as much as I do.

results.title: The Reluctant Prophet
results.description: Like Jonah, you know God's truth but struggle to embrace it when it costs you personally — especially when it involves extending grace to people you believe don't deserve it. You're honest about your feelings (sometimes brutally so), and you have deep theological convictions. But there's a gap between what you believe in your head and what you practice with your heart. The good news? God gave Jonah a second chance, and He'll give you one too. The question is whether you'll take it.
strengths: Theological depth and biblical knowledge
Unflinching honesty about your feelings with God
Willingness to eventually obey, even reluctantly
Capacity for powerful, raw prayer in crisis moments
watchFor: Resentment when God blesses people you think don't deserve it
Confusing personal preferences with God's will
Caring more about comfort than about souls
Obeying outwardly while harboring bitterness inwardly

scripture.text: I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abounding in love, a God who relents from sending calamity.

results.title: The Practical Responder
results.description: Like the ship captain, you are pragmatic, action-oriented, and morally courageous. When a crisis hits, you don't freeze — you act. You exhaust every practical option before appealing to the supernatural, and you show genuine concern for the people in your care. You may not have deep theological training, but your instincts are often more spiritually attuned than you realize. Your challenge is moving from crisis-mode faith to everyday intimacy with God.
strengths: Natural leadership in crisis situations
Genuine concern for the well-being of others
Willingness to try every option, including prayer
Moral integrity that values human life above convenience
watchFor: Relying on your own competence before turning to God
Treating faith as a last resort rather than a first response
Spiritual openness that lacks depth or commitment
Being so action-focused that you miss the deeper spiritual lesson

scripture.text: The captain went to him and said, 'How can you sleep? Get up and call on your god! Maybe he will take notice of us so that we will not perish.'

results.title: The Faithful Instrument
results.description: Like the great fish, you are quietly obedient, available, and willing to play whatever role God assigns — even if it seems strange, uncomfortable, or unrecognized. You don't need the spotlight. You don't need applause. You show up, do what God asks, and trust that your obedience is part of a bigger story you may never fully see. Your greatest strength is your availability. Your challenge is trusting that silent faithfulness matters as much as visible ministry.
strengths: Quiet, consistent obedience without needing recognition
Availability to God for unusual or uncomfortable assignments
Patient endurance through dark, difficult seasons
Trust in God's bigger plan even when your role seems small
watchFor: Passivity disguised as patience — God also calls us to initiative
Undervaluing your own role in God's story
Difficulty expressing your needs or struggles to others
Accepting discomfort without discerning whether God is calling you to change

scripture.text: Now the Lord provided a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish three days and three nights.

results.title: The Wholehearted Repenter
results.description: Like the king of Nineveh, you respond to God's word with immediate, radical, public action. When conviction strikes, you don't negotiate, delay, or manage appearances — you throw off your royal robes, sit in the dust, and lead others to do the same. Your humility is genuine, your repentance is thorough, and your leadership inspires others to turn toward God. Your greatest strength is your willingness to be publicly vulnerable. Your challenge is sustaining that intensity beyond the initial moment of conviction.
strengths: Immediate responsiveness to God's conviction
Willingness to be publicly humble and vulnerable
Leadership that inspires others toward repentance and faith
Deep hope in God's mercy even when you don't deserve it
watchFor: Emotional intensity that fades once the crisis passes
Confusing dramatic gestures with sustained transformation
Leading others into repentance without modeling ongoing discipleship
Presuming upon God's mercy rather than maintaining humble dependence

scripture.text: Who knows? God may yet relent and with compassion turn from his fierce anger so that we will not perish.

results.title: The Compassionate Pursuer
results.description: You reflect God's heart in the book of Jonah — a heart that sees the big picture, pursues the lost relentlessly, and extends mercy even when others think it's undeserved. You have deep compassion for people others have written off, and you are patient with those who are still learning, still struggling, still running. Your greatest strength is your wide mercy. Your challenge is that compassion fatigue is real, and even the most generous heart needs to be replenished by God's Spirit to keep giving what others need.
strengths: Wide, inclusive compassion that extends to unlikely people
Patient persistence with people who are slow to change
Ability to see the bigger picture beyond personal hurt
Genuine joy when the lost are found and the broken are restored
watchFor: Compassion fatigue from carrying others' burdens too long
Neglecting your own spiritual nourishment while caring for others
Frustration with people who limit God's mercy to their own preferences
The temptation to enable harmful behavior in the name of grace

scripture.text: And should I not have concern for the great city of Nineveh, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand people who cannot tell their right hand from their left — and also many animals?
